summary: An early-1900s lookout site in southwest Oregon got its current 1952 L-4 tower, which was staffed into the 1990s and again in 2007 but now sits idle and closed to reservations.

facts.status_note: Recreation.gov listing says the rental is closed to reservations until further notice; Firelookout.com describes it as presently abandoned after use into the early 2010s.

access.note: A Forest Service recreation rental, but currently closed to reservations; when open, access is by key pickup from the Wild Rivers Ranger District office in Grants Pass.

visit.trail_note: Eight miles of gravel road off Riverbanks Road south of Grants Pass; not recommended for families with toddlers because of the tower.

events.note: First lookout: a 20-foot platform tower, developed about 1915-1916.
A D-6 cupola replaced the platform tower.
An Aircraft Warning Service observation cabin was built on site.
Present 10-12 foot treated-timber L-4 tower built.
Staffed into the 1990s, per NHLR and Firelookout.com.
Firelookout.com says the lookout was staffed again in 2007 after a stint on the rental program.
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register September 1, 2001.

evidence.supports: build history and 1952 tower, staffed into 1990s
evidence.quote: Developed about 1915 with a 20' platform tower, a D-6 cupola replaced it in 1924. An Aircraft Warning Service cabin was built in 1942. The present 10' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1952, was staffed into the 1990s. It is available on the Recreation Rental program.

evidence.supports: rental, 2007 restaffing, use into early 2010s, now abandoned
evidence.quote: It was made available on the Recreation Rental program, but staffed again in 2007. It was still in use into the early 2010s but is presently abandoned.

evidence.supports: closed to reservations, 1915 platform tower, 1924 cabin, 1942 cabin, 1952 structure
evidence.quote: THIS FACILITY IS CLOSED TO RESERVATIONS UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE ... The original Onion Mountain Lookout was a raised platform, built on top of a tower in 1916. In 1924, a second lookout without a tower was built on site. The current structure was placed on site in 1952 and served as a fire lookout and Aircraft Warning Service observation station.

evidence.supports: access directions and key pickup, family suitability
evidence.quote: Entry to the lookout is by a key. Please call the Wild Rivers Ranger District office at 541-471-6500, four days prior to arrival to arrange pick up and drop off of the key.
Because of the tower on the site, this rental is not recommended for families with toddlers or young children
Oregon Caves National Monument is within a hour's drive.

From Grants Pass travel Highway 199 south to Riverbanks Road ... Proceed on Riverbanks Road, 5.5 miles to Shan Creek Road and turn left. Travel 8 miles on this gravel road to Forest Service Road 2509 and turn right. ... Onion Mountain Lookout is accessible by car, but the last 8.75 miles are on graveled Forest Service roads.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Firelookout.com give 1915 for the first platform tower; Recreation.gov gives 1916. Both years are noted as approximate in the sources themselves, so the story uses 'around 1915 or 1916.'

notes_for_editor: Current rental is closed to reservations (confirmed live on Recreation.gov as of 2026-10-04), consistent with Firelookout.com's note that the site is presently abandoned; treated access as 'restricted' rather than fully 'public' to flag that. Minor year discrepancy on the first platform tower (1915 vs 1916).
